# `apprafter lock`

Lock this target store's secrets in an encrypted vault, or put them back in files. On a locked store, a command that needs a Hetzner token or a cached kubeconfig asks for the lock password in its terminal, and is refused where there is no terminal: an AI agent that runs `apprafter` as you cannot use them without you. Other target stores on this computer are not changed

```text
Usage: apprafter lock <COMMAND>
```

Subcommands:

- [`apprafter lock now`](#apprafter-lock-now) — End the unlock window in this terminal now.
- [`apprafter lock off`](#apprafter-lock-off) — Put this target store's secrets back on disk in clear — readable by any program running as you — and delete the vault.
- [`apprafter lock on`](#apprafter-lock-on) — Move this target store's secrets into an encrypted vault: its targets' Hetzner tokens, a new age key of its own, and the cached kubeconfigs and Argo CD passwords re-encrypted to it.
- [`apprafter lock status`](#apprafter-lock-status) — Whether this target store is locked, how it opens (its slots), the unlock window left in this terminal, and what this computer lets other programs running as you do

## `apprafter lock now`

End the unlock window in this terminal now. Asks nothing

```text
Usage: apprafter lock now
```

Examples:

```sh
apprafter lock now
```

## `apprafter lock off`

Put this target store's secrets back on disk in clear — readable by any program running as you — and delete the vault. Asks for the lock password or the recovery key, even inside an unlock window. Also backs out of an interrupted `apprafter lock on`

```text
Usage: apprafter lock off
```

Examples:

```sh
apprafter lock off
```

## `apprafter lock on`

Move this target store's secrets into an encrypted vault: its targets' Hetzner tokens, a new age key of its own, and the cached kubeconfigs and Argo CD passwords re-encrypted to it. By default the vault opens with your account password on this computer, checked with the system once, now (Linux, macOS), and with a recovery key shown once, which you type back. Where this computer cannot check the account password — and on Windows, until AppRafter supports Windows Hello there — it asks for a new lock password twice instead, and says why. Run it again to finish an interrupted run; on a locked store, `--timeout` changes the default unlock window

```text
Usage: apprafter lock on [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Value | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--lock-password` | flag | — | no | Protect the store with a separate lock password instead of your account password: asked twice, only AppRafter's prompt ever sees it; then a recovery key is shown once, which you type back. Use it on a computer where an agent gets your account password, or for a store you use on more than one computer |
| `--timeout` | `<MINUTES>` | — | no | Minutes an unlock window stays open by default, restarted by each command that uses it; 0 makes every command ask. Default 5 |

Examples:

```sh
apprafter lock on
apprafter lock on --lock-password
apprafter lock on --timeout 15
```

## `apprafter lock status`

Whether this target store is locked, how it opens (its slots), the unlock window left in this terminal, and what this computer lets other programs running as you do

```text
Usage: apprafter lock status
```

Examples:

```sh
apprafter lock status
```
